Hi Samira — thanks for the concrete examples, they help a lot. Below is a concise ledgerization and rounding summary plus a worked example for the rows you sent. I pasted the short version here and attached a CSV with the per-row mapping to invoice lines.

High-level rules (current Redwood billing model for hosted & dedicated):
- Raw tokens: counted exactly by tokenizer per request (includes prompt + response).
- Billing quantum: per-request billed units = ceil(raw_tokens / billing_quantum) * billing_quantum. Default billing_quantum = 100 tokens for per-call (REST) endpoints.
- Conversation bundling: when requests are grouped into an "active conversation window" (configurable, default 24 hours), we apply conversation-level amortization: the sum(raw_tokens) across the window is totaled and then quantized once using the billing_quantum. This avoids double-rounding small back-and-forth calls.
- Model switching: billing is attached to the request that executed. If you switch models mid-conversation, each request bills against whichever runtime handled it. However, if the requests are part of the same active conversation window and you enable "bundle-amortize=true", we sum tokens across both models and apply a single quantization step. The invoice will show per-request model attribution but the billed_units reflect the amortized quantization.
- Sustained streams (>5000 raw tokens): we switch to proportional quantization to avoid unfair ceiling effects. Billed_units = max(ceil(raw_tokens / 100) * 100, round_to_nearest( raw_tokens, 10 ) ) for long streams; effectively we round to the nearest 10 tokens above the 5k threshold.
- Prefix/KV cache reuse: when KV caching detects identical prefix tokens between requests, we do not double-bill those tokens in the amortized window. The ledger will indicate raw_token_count and cache_reuse_flag so you can see when tokens were omitted from billed totals.

Worked example (based on your attached 6-row sample):
- Row 1: raw_tokens=180 -> billed_units=200 (ceil(180/100)*100)
- Row 2: raw_tokens=45 (follow-up within same 24h window) -> amortized_total_window = 180+45=225 -> billed_units_window = 300 -> if both requests are bundled, individual invoice lines will show 180/45 attribution with a single billed_total=300 (split by ratio on invoice)
- Row 3 (model switch): raw_tokens=120 on m1, raw_tokens=250 on m2 -> if not bundled, billed=200 and 300 respectively; if bundled with bundle-amortize=true, sum=370 -> billed_units=400 and invoice will annotate model attribution custom field.
- Row 4 (stream): raw_tokens=5200 -> billed_units ~ 5200 rounded to nearest 10 => 5200 (no extra ceiling).

I'll attach the per-row ledger CSV mapping and a short example invoice snippet for clarity. If you'd like formal language for procurement/POs we can also attach the pricing terms excerpt.

Action items:

- If you'd like, we can toggle bundle-amortize for the pilot so you avoid per-call rounding for interactive chat flows.
